messages:
eden_sales: Heads-up — Stratus POC hitting slow first-token and sporadic 429s during their daytime load test. They see TTFTs of 800-1,200ms on small prompts and occasional 429 bursts. Started a run at 09:05 PT.

lina_sales: +1, they're on Dedicated trial. High priority for the account. They asked about warmup and prefill behaviors.

akshay_se: Can you paste a sample request profile and the model + config? Also any error snippets from the client.

eden_sales: Sample request (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
model: redwood-2.1.x-16q
auth: token
payload: {"prompt": "Summarize...", "max_tokens": 120}
headers: {"x-client-id": "stratus-poc"}
```
Client logs show: 
- 429 x 3 over 90s (retry succeeding)
- TTFT ~ 850-1250ms

marta_support: Do we know the Dedicated pool size and prefill policy? 429s could be from per-customer throttles or shard queueing.

jun_sre: I checked the cluster telemetry: their dedicated pool has 2 x A100 nodes, batch window set to 20ms, concurrent_slots=8, prefill_policy=disabled. KV cache hit rate is very low for this workload (~12%).

akshay_se: Prefill disabled is likely causing the early-token lag. For small prompts prefill/warmup matters because tokens/kv cache empty -> kernel warmup + IO. Can they enable a small prefill or increase concurrent_slots?

lina_sales: They were worried about billing blowup with prefill. Also raised pricing Q: how is prefill charged — is it full token billing?

akshay_se: Prefill counts toward tokens used but we can recommend a short strategy: prefill with 8-16 tokens per concurrent session, or use an aggressive KV cache TTL so subsequent requests hit. Also suggest model quantization profile: 8-bit int8q to reduce latency.

tom_se: Quick reproducible test: can we run a synthetic load that simulates their daytime ramp (200 rps peak, 60% concurrency)? If 429s persist, we need to look at shard queue lengths and rate-limiter logs.

jun_sre: I'll tail the relevant logs now. If you trigger a ramp I can correlate traces. Also will check per-customer route limiter: service.ratelimiter.customer.stratus-poc.*

eden_sales: Running a ramp from their side in 2m. Notifying Stratus.

deploy-bot: warmup-job started for pool=dedicated-42, job_id=wk-20240421-07, prefill_tokens=12

marta_support: Thanks — two asks for the customer: 1) Would you allow a 1-minute prefill test (12 tokens) so we can measure TTFT improvement? 2) Can you provide a short sample trace when you hit 429 (timestamp + request id)?

stratus-cust (via eden_sales): ok to 1-minute prefill test. Will send sample request-id when 429s show up.

jun_sre: After warmup started I see a drop in median TTFT from ~950ms -> ~420ms for new sessions. KV cache hit climbed to ~68% on prefills. Still seeing isolated 429 spikes correlated with short 5s bursts. Traces show queue_depth spiking on shard-3: queue_depth 28 -> 62 at 09:12:14.

akshay_se: Queue spikes likely due to affinity/queueing imbalance. Recommend enabling soft prefill + adjust batch_window down to 10ms for this workload. Also tune routing policy to spread requests across more shards (route_policy=balanced).

lina_sales: I'll draft a one-pager for Stratus with the suggested config and a billing note: "prefill tokens billed as normal usage; we can cap prefill duration for POC to limit cost".

eden_sales: Customer asks whether we can set an explicit fallback policy if a shard's queue_depth > 40 to route to a warm spare. Is that supported?

jun_sre: We have automated fallback rules but not per-customer threshold toggles via Console yet. For now we can create a route override: route_rule { if queue_depth>40 -> route: pool-ephemeral } — I can push that for the POC.

marta_support: Action items: Jun to push temporary route override + monitor; Akshay to provide prefill + batch_window recommendation and cost estimate; Lina to send the PO C one-pager and pricing note; Eden to coordinate customer ramp and collect 429 trace ids.

eden_sales: Thanks all — will follow up after the next 30m ramp. :thumbsup:
